answer: An operator's clones share one room, one clock and one feed, so make locality cost: at unpredictable moments each identity must report the fine grain of its claimed place - the umber tint of river silt after rain, which walnut trees on its street have dropped their nuts, the water level at its oasis - and neighbours' reports must interlock on the same transient details. A farm in one datacentre either copies one report, exposing identical grain across names, or invents many, and invented grains disagree with the real neighbours who were actually there.
